info.name: FOFA API
info.description:
Postman collection for the FOFA cyberspace mapping API (https://en.fofa.info/api/v1), including ready-to-run hunting queries taken from the FofaInfo/Awesome-FOFA guides (https://github.com/FofaInfo/Awesome-FOFA).

## Setup
1. Select the **FOFA** environment (top-right). It holds `fofa_key`, which is sent automatically as the `key` query parameter through the collection-level API Key auth.
2. Run **API Reference > Account Information** first to confirm the key works.

## How queries work
- Generic requests (API Reference folder) read the plain-text FOFA query from the collection variable `query`. The collection pre-request script Base64-encodes it (UTF-8, URL-safe) into `{{qbase64}}`.
- Every saved hunting request has its own pre-request script with the plain query in `const q = String.raw`...``. Edit that line to change the query; the script encodes it for you.
- Hunting requests use `full=true` because most IOCs in the guides are from 2023-2024 and fall outside FOFA's default one-year window.

## Folders
- **API Reference**: every documented endpoint.
- **Fuzzy Search**: wildcard syntax (`*=` with `*` and `?`).
- **Threat Intel Discovery Guide**: header, banner, port, JARM and certificate pivoting plus false-positive reduction.
- **APT - COLDRIVER** and **APT - Sidewinder**: step-by-step IOC expansion exactly as in the guides.
- **Other Guides**: ObserverStealer, APT Bitter, APT-C-23, Silver Fox, Ducktail, DeepSeek impersonation, certificate filtering, supply chain, beginner examples and FofaHub.

## Limits and permissions
- Keep the overall rate below 2 requests/second. Stats: 1 request every 5 s. Host: 1 request/s.
- `size` max 10,000 (2,000 when fields include cert/banner, 500 when they include body).
- Fuzzy search (`*=`) needs a Personal membership or higher (or F-points). Some fields (header_hash, product, icon_hash, body, fid...) need paid tiers; the default field sets here only use free fields.
- Hunting results are leads, not verdicts: cross-check them on threat-intel platforms (VirusTotal, ThreatBook, Qianxin) as the guides recommend.

item.name: API Reference

request.description:
GET /search/all - asset search with page-based pagination.

Set the plain-text FOFA query in the `query` collection variable; it is Base64-encoded automatically.

Parameters: `qbase64` (required), `fields` (default host,ip,port), `page` (default 1), `size` (default 100, max 10,000), `full` (true = all history, false = last year), `r_type=json`.

exec: console.log('Next cursor saved to next_id: ' + j.next);

request.description:
GET /search/next - cursor-based pagination that avoids data misalignment on large pulls.

On the first call leave `next_id` empty. The test script stores the returned cursor in `next_id`, so just send again for the next page. Clear `next_id` to restart.
Documentation example with a fixed qbase64 for ip="103.35.168.38" (does not use the `query` variable).

GET /search/stats - top 5 values of each requested field for the query. Limit: 1 request every 5 s.

Supported fields: protocol, domain, port, title, os, server, country, asn, org, asset_type, fid, icp.

`distinct` returns unique counts for server, domain, title, fid.
GET /host/{host} - host summary (ports, protocols, domains, categories, products). Limit: 1 request/s.
GET /host/{host}?detail=true - per-port detail with products, category, level (5 application, 4 support, 3 service, 2 system, 1 hardware, 0 N/A) and hardware flag.

exec: console.log(`User: ${j.username} | VIP: ${j.isvip} (level ${j.vip_level}) | Remaining queries: ${j.remain_api_query} | Remaining data: ${j.remain_api_data}`);

item.description:
Source: *The correct way to use Fuzzy Search in FOFA*.

Fuzzy search is enabled with `*=` (the operator itself is not a wildcard). Inside the value:
- `*` matches zero, one or many characters
- `?` matches exactly one character

Originally built to fix incomplete word segmentation (e.g. a MySQL banner containing `0ubuntu0` would not match `ubuntu`).

Requires Personal membership or higher, or F-points.

item.name: Threat Intel Discovery Guide

exec: const q = String.raw`org="BLNWX" && header="Location: http://www.google.com" && header="Server: nginx/1.18.0 (Ubuntu)" && domain!=""`;

request.description: Header-based association from HEDnsExtractor + httpx output: same ASN org, redirect to google.com, nginx 1.18.0 on Ubuntu, non-empty domain. The guide reports 33 unique IPs.
Used in the guide to show that a C2 JARM match does not mean the service is C2. Compare the JARM values returned here with a pure JARM search: JARM is only an auxiliary signal.
Step 1 of the port-based example: collect the router family through its favicon hash. Contains false positives on its own.

item.name: Port pivot - compromised router check (per IP)

request.description: Step 2: for each IP from the previous request, check whether port 22 is open with banner `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_6.7p2` (the APT's implant signature). Set the `host` collection variable to the IP to test. The guide does this in bulk with `fofa search -i ips.txt --template ...` (GoFOFA).
Anti-pattern: returns hundreds of millions of assets (316,493,580 in the guide). A feature without uniqueness cannot attribute anything. Use Statistic Aggregation if you only want the count.

request.description:
Template with a high false-positive rate (tens of thousands). The guide pipes the results to httpx and keeps hosts where `/api/check` returns 200 with content length 355:

`... | httpx -path /api/check -sc -cl -mc 200 -ml 355`

Note: `header_hash` filtering requires a Personal membership or higher.

Host Aggregation on the initial OceanLotus IOC from the guide (tagged by ThreatBook and Qianxin).

item.description:
Source: *A Comprehensive Guide to Threat Intelligence Discovery Using FOFA*.

Workflow: input source (known group or known IOC) -> confirm attribution on TI platforms -> extract common IOC features -> build FOFA syntax -> remove false positives -> verify.

Feature priority: 1) certificate, 2) TLS fingerprint (JARM / JA3S), 3) HTTP header, 4) banner. Ports help for hard-coded RAT callbacks.

False-positive signals: tens of thousands of results, domestic IPs for a foreign group, last-update dates far from the activity window, and under 30% coverage on TI platforms. Fix by adding fields / intersecting clues, path collision (httpx), or reverse engineering.

item.description:
Source: *Practical FOFA Asset Discovery: COLDRIVER*.

COLDRIVER (UNC4057, Star Blizzard, Callisto) is a Russian group doing credential phishing against NGOs, former intelligence/military officers and NATO government figures.

Initial IOC (Google TAG, 18 Jan 2024): C2 `45.133.216.15:3000`, path `/ws`.

Run the requests in order: each step adds a feature to cut false positives. Final result in the guide: 3 IPs (the known C2 + 2 suspicious), all seen Aug-Oct 2023, matching the group's active window.

item.description:
Source: *Practical FOFA Asset Expansion: Sidewinder APT*.

Seed IOCs: neger.site, semain.tech, aliit.org (maltrail / Bridewell) and direct888.net, fia-gov.net (@Cyberteam008).

Method: look up each IOC, notice the shared JARM, discard JARM alone (247,319 results), then add the common 404 nginx headers and Content-Length values. The three final rules returned 193 results in the guide; coverage was Qianxin 137, ThreatBook 118, VirusTotal 138, and 24 not covered by any.

The group spoofs government domains (`*fia-gov*`, `*mofa-gov*`, `*govpk*`) and uses typo/shifted names (`direct888`, `directt88`, `downlod`).

try { json = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { json = null; }
